findings.consumer_location: src/builtin_tools/web_fetch/mod.rs:151-189 — field is read but the block deliberately logs and falls through to the built-in safe_fetch (the SSRF-DNS-pin gap, BT-D-R4-22). The only live caller of FetchProvider::fetch() is src/gateway/handlers/fetch_config.rs:413,447 (handle_test, hardcoded https://example.com). Constructor wires them in: src/executor/builtin_registry/builder/constructor/mod.rs:73.
findings.rationale: The producer (FetchProvider trait + Crawl4aiFetchProvider + FirecrawlFetchProvider + FetchRegistry + factory + FirecrawlFetchProvider's /v2/scrape plumbing) is fully implemented and tested, the constructor (executor/builtin_registry/builder/constructor/mod.rs:72-73) wires the registry's `select()` into `WebFetchTool::with_fetch_providers(...)`, but `WebFetchTool::call_impl` (web_fetch/mod.rs:151-189) deliberately SKIPS the configured providers and falls through to the built-in safe_fetch because the DNS pin cannot be threaded into a provider's own reqwest client. So the wire is intact at construction time but the runtime consumer is a no-op log line. Per the painless-wire heuristic: zero observed production pain because the built-in reqwest path covers the agent-facing fetch, and the only genuine consumer is the connection-test RPC. The comment in src/fetch/provider.rs:14-26 explicitly documents this as 'BT-D-R4-22 ... until DNS pin plumbing lands.' Two viable paths: (a) keep dormant scaffolding awaiting the planned DNS-pin fix, or (b) CUT the field + builder + registry.select() + factory + 3 impls and keep only Crawl4aiFetchProvider / FirecrawlFetchProvider for the connection-test RPC. The CUT path requires relocating the two providers into `gateway/handlers/fetch_config.rs` (their only real caller) and would shrink the public surface by ~5 files. Recommend DECIDE — this is a product/scheduling call, not an audit-tactical cut.
findings.residual_risk: If kept dormant: operators who set `[fetch].backends.crawl4ai` expect providers to be consulted; the silent skip will surprise them until DNS-pin plumbing lands.

findings.consumer_location: src/fetch/registry.rs:31, :54 (FetchProviderFactoryRegistry::with_defaults() then factories.get(...).build(...)). No external callers anywhere in src/, tests/, interfaces/, desktop/, bindings/, crates/.
findings.rationale: Strictly speaking these have a live internal consumer (FetchRegistry::from_config), so they are not Form-1 dead code — the trait indirection is load-bearing because FirecrawlFetchFactory returns None when [search].firecrawl isn't configured and Crawl4aiFetchFactory performs the token-precedence lookup. BUT: they are `pub` (factory.rs declares `pub trait`, `pub struct` x3) yet no crate outside src/fetch/ ever imports, constructs, or implements them. The pub surface is wider than necessary; the trait is functionally a single-call dispatch table used once at registry construction. If the wider audit concludes sw-fetch-2-1 with CUT, these four symbols become dead and should be deleted. If sw-fetch-2-1 is KEPT, recommend demoting to `pub(crate)` (or inlining the two factories into FetchRegistry::from_config) so external crates cannot depend on an abstraction that exists only to serve one internal call site.
findings.residual_risk: If any future consumer (e.g. a third fetch backend: 'jina', 'tavily') is planned, the factory abstraction earns its keep; otherwise the trait is over-engineered for two impls.

findings.consumer_location: none — the only `.is_available()` calls are the trait's own dummy test (src/fetch/provider.rs:61). FetchRegistry::select() does not consult it; WebFetchTool does not consult it. Contrast src/search/registry.rs:515 and :677 which DO consult SearchProvider::is_available() in selection paths.
findings.rationale: Both concrete providers implement is_available() — Crawl4aiFetchProvider::is_available synchronously probes the backend's health endpoint, FirecrawlFetchProvider::is_available returns base_url/api_key non-empty — but neither registry nor consumer ever calls it. This is a real asymmetry vs the sibling search category (src/search/registry.rs:515, :677 filter on is_available). Either the fetch registry should call it in select() (treating the trait method as a per-provider readiness gate), or the trait should be reduced to fetch+name. Decide based on whether the planned DNS-pin plumbing will land and whether a per-provider readiness gate would help that path; otherwise CUT.
findings.residual_risk: Trivial: dead method on a public trait is dead_code-lint clean because the impls use it (LintCPS: impl method satisfies the trait method).

findings.consumer_location: none — no file or document named `firecrawl_scrape_response_ignores_success_field` exists anywhere in the repo (rg across .rs/.md returns only the comment that names it). The fix (bubbling success=false) is real and tested (tests at firecrawl.rs:175-185), so the *behaviour* is not severed; only the *pointer* to the audit notes is orphaned.
findings.rationale: Stale cross-reference. The comment claims an external audit-note file documents the bug; no such file exists. Replace with a self-contained rationale, e.g. `// Firecrawl v2 returns HTTP 200 with success=false for quota/auth/blocked-page outcomes; surfacing the upstream error verbatim (see map_scrape below and the success_false_surfaces_upstream_error test).` This is a pure documentation hygiene fix.

verification: Static only per instructions — cargo check/test intentionally NOT run. All evidence is rg/grep across src/, tests/, interfaces/, desktop/, crates/, bindings/, build.rs, shared/, docs/.
notes: Module is small (5 producers + 7 impls + 6 concrete provider functions). The dominant finding is structural: the fetch-provider category is implemented as a full trait/factory/registry pipeline that mirrors the search category, but only the connection-test RPC (gateway/handlers/fetch_config.rs::handle_test) actually exercises the provider's `fetch()` method in production — the agent-facing web_fetch path deliberately bypasses it. This is well-documented (BT-D-R4-22 across web_fetch/mod.rs:152,181,649,691; provider.rs:14-26; firecrawl.rs:97-110) and is awaiting DNS-pin plumbing to close. sw-fetch-2-1 is the highest-signal finding: it scopes roughly half the module (`FetchProvider` +2 impls + factory + registry + WebFetchTool::fetch_providers + the constructor wiring) as dormant scaffolding pending one engineering fix. sw-fetch-1-1 and sw-fetch-1-2 are subtler code smells (over-public factory surface; dead trait method) that are independently CUT-eligible and become strongly CUT-eligible if sw-fetch-2-1 is CUT. sw-fetch-3-1 and sw-fetch-3-2 are pure doc/comment hygiene.
